segments.text: American Fork City Council — Regular Session — January 22, 2019:

entities.speaker: Bradley J. Frost
entities.remark-context: NAACP Outstanding Community Service Award for Officer Diego Garcia

segments.text: Mayor Frost recognized Officer Diego Garcia for receiving the NAACP Outstanding Community Service Award, described examples of Garcia’s community work, and thanked Garcia and the Police Department for their service.

entities.speaker: David H. Bunker
entities.remark-context: Recognition of police and fire service

segments.text: City Administrator Bunker thanked Officer Garcia and the police and fire departments, and recalled an occasion when officers acted exceptionally and saved lives.

entities.speaker: Barbara Christiansen
entities.remark-context: Recognition of police and fire service

segments.text: Council Member Christiansen thanked Officer Garcia and the police and fire departments for their service.
Council Member Shelton encouraged the city to consider new dispatch technology that he said could reduce response times, and he thanked Officer Garcia for his service.

entities.speaker: Kevin J. Barnes
entities.remark-context: Recognition of police and fire service

segments.text: Council Member Barnes thanked Officer Garcia and the police and fire departments, noting that many people contribute to the city’s operation.
Council Member Taylor thanked the Police Department for its service and reported having a positive experience with the city’s Emergency Operations Center.

entities.speaker: Kyle Maurer
entities.remark-context: Lease agreement for six police vehicles

segments.text: Responding to a question about financing six police vehicles, Kyle Maurer explained that the proposed master lease would establish termination provisions and operate similarly to an automobile loan.

entities.speaker: David H. Bunker
entities.remark-context: Public-safety services contract with Cedar Hills

segments.text: During discussion of public-safety services for Cedar Hills, City Administrator Bunker explained that the police-services portion was a two-year contract with a 3% increase after two years and a 180-day termination provision.

entities.label: Officer Diego Garcia recognition and police service

segments.text: Mayor Frost recognized Officer Diego Garcia’s NAACP Outstanding Community Service Award, followed by additional comments recognizing Garcia and police service.
Relevant discussion from the official meeting minutes:

Mayor Frost invited Officer Garcia and his family to the front of the room. Officer Garcia was awarded the NAACP Outstanding Community Service Award. Mayor Frost gave some examples of Officer Garcia’s work in the community. He thanked him and the police department for their service.

Mr. Bunker thanked Officer Garcia, the police department and the fire department for their service. He shared a story of when the officers acted exceptionally and saved lives.

Council Member Christiansen also thanked the police and fire departments for their service.

Council Member Shelton reported that he was able to preview new technology. This technology was revolutionizing dispatch services by reducing response times. He asked that the Council consider implementing it in the City. He also thanked Officer Garcia for his service.

Council Member Barnes also thanked Officer Garcia, the police department, and the fire department. He stated it took many people to make the City run efficiently.

Council Member Taylor thanked the police department for their service. He reported that he had a good experience with the EOC.

entities.label: Lease financing for six police vehicles

segments.text: During consideration of financing six police vehicles, Kyle Maurer explained how the proposed master lease would operate.
Relevant discussion from the official meeting minutes:
When asked by Council Member Shelton what a master lease was, Mr. Maurer explained it was a leasing agreement that would set the terms for the out-clauses. It was structured like an auto loan.
The broader agenda item covered public-safety contracts with Cedar Hills. This excerpt retains the portion specifically explaining the police-services agreement.
Relevant discussion from the official meeting minutes:
Council Member Carroll asked how the police service was structured. Mr. Bunker responded it was a two-year contract with a 3% increase at the end of the two years. It also had the 180-day clause.
